nodes.summary: Let $f_m(n)$ be the number of maximal sum-free subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$. Then $f_m(n) / 2^{n/2} \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$, that is, $f_m(n) = o(2^{n/2})$.
nodes.title: Maximal sum-free subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ number $o(2^{n/2})$

nodes.summary: Let $f_m(n)$ be the number of maximal sum-free subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$. This is the statement, asked by Cameron and Erdős, that $f_m(n) / 2^{n/2} \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$, that is, $f_m(n) = o(2^{n/2})$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 877 on maximal sum-free sets

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $f_m(n)$ is the number of sets $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ that are sum-free, meaning $x + y \notin A$ for all $x, y \in A$ (including $x = y$), and maximal with this property: every sum-free set $B$ with $A \subseteq B \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ equals $A$.
nodes.title: Number of maximal sum-free subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$

nodes.summary: Let $f(n)$ be the number of sum-free subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$, that is, of sets $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ with no $a, b, c \in A$ satisfying $a = b + c$ (the case $b = c$ included). Then $\log_2 f(n) / n \to 1/2$ as $n \to \infty$, that is, $f(n) = 2^{(1 + o(1)) n / 2}$.
nodes.title: Sum-free subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ number $2^{(1 + o(1)) n / 2}$

nodes.summary: Let $f(n)$ be the number of sum-free subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$. This is the statement that $\log_2 f(n) / n \to 1/2$ as $n \to \infty$, that is, $f(n) = 2^{(1 + o(1)) n / 2}$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 748 on the number of sum-free sets

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $f(n)$ is the number of sets $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ that are sum-free, meaning that there are no $a, b, c \in A$ with $a = b + c$ (the case $b = c$ included). The empty set is counted.
nodes.title: Number of sum-free subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$

can_prove.label: ready to prove

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
